# Embedded tracing measurement, October 17, 2026

All 20 original cells completed and passed their business, resource and export
audits. **None of the four CPU-budget criteria qualifies.** This is an unreleased
embedded candidate measurement, with no stable, service-mode or capacity claim.

## Method and software

The [method was recorded before results](https://github.com/durable-workflow/workflow/issues/773#issuecomment-6228453784).
The [functional and offered-load prerequisites](https://github.com/durable-workflow/workflow/issues/773#issuecomment-6228327954)
are separate observations. This batch ran three rotating matched repetitions
of published Workflow 2.5.28, candidate tracing disabled, and candidate tracing
enabled. Two final published-baseline cells checked drift. Every cell used fresh
application/database state and the same four workers, logging call, dependency
references, resource limits and local accepting collector.

Measured candidate: `316316a827fadc7b5aa545842451ca9c8e7a9db5`, tree
`c5ac80029a831e2664200e8b58aa301e657053dd`. Published source matched all 606
files at tag `592dee`; other dependency references matched the candidate.
This compares the complete candidate with the published package. It does not
isolate every candidate change as a causal tracing cost.

The dedicated amd64 host had eight logical CPUs, about 16 GiB RAM, AMD EPYC-Rome
as observed, Microsoft hypervisor, Linux 6.8.0-146 and cgroup v2. Docker was
29.1.3, Compose 2.40.3, PHP 8.3.35 with pcntl, Redis extension 6.1.0 and CLI
OPcache disabled. Builds and dependency installation finished before measurement.
Administrative SSH/status reads and one bounded first-cell reader-validation
copy occurred during the batch. No concurrent build or unrelated application
workload was admitted. This is not a matched hardware performance claim against
another product or an estimate of maximum capacity.

| Role | CPU cap | Memory cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HTTP application | 0.5 | 512 MiB |
| Each of four workers | 1 | 384 MiB |
| MySQL | 1 | 2 GiB |
| Redis | 0.1 | 128 MiB |
| Collector | 0.2 | 256 MiB |
| Probe | 0.2 | 256 MiB |

Swap was disabled. The primary quantity is the sum of exact CPU counter deltas
from all nine containers, divided by measured completed workflows. It includes
application, all workers, database, cache, collector and probe through child
completion/provider drain. Setup, warmup, audit queries, host sampling tools and
teardown are outside those deltas. Every container identity, cap and counter
interval was checked before/after. No OOM, restart or nonzero child exit occurred.

Ordinary cells offered one one-activity workflow per second for 120 seconds,
120 measured completions. Fan-out cells offered one 64-activity workflow per
minute for 120 seconds, two measured completions. Separate warmups completed
30 ordinary workflows or one fan-out workflow before measurement. Original
90-second observer, 100-second run and 120-second execution bounds were retained.
Providers were installed in every cell. The application registered the log tap
only in the enabled profile, as described in the [recipe](README.md).

## CPU acceptance

Each estimate is the mean of three matched candidate/baseline ratios, with a
two-sided 95% paired-t interval, n=3, df=2. The frozen acceptance requires both
the upper interval endpoint and absolute final baseline drift to fit the target.
Negative point estimates do not demonstrate a speed improvement.

| Workload | Profile | Mean CPU change | 95% interval | Baseline drift | Target | Qualified |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Ordinary | Disabled | -1.28% | [-6.15%, +3.60%] | +0.30% | 1% | No |
| Ordinary | Enabled | +6.26% | [+3.16%, +9.36%] | +0.30% | 5% | No |
| 64-member fan-out | Disabled | -1.28% | [-8.27%, +5.70%] | +4.10% | 1% | No |
| 64-member fan-out | Enabled | +0.43% | [-12.20%, +13.07%] | +4.10% | 5% | No |

## Latency, memory and correctness

All declared offers were accepted and completed, with no missed offer or HTTP
error. Per-cell observed completion rates were about 0.9960–1.00001 workflows/s
for ordinary work and 0.0166665–0.0166668 for fan-out. These are offered-load
results. Fan-out has only two measured observations per cell, so its high
percentiles describe those few observations, not a reliable tail distribution.

Each latency entry is the arithmetic mean of three per-cell percentiles, in
milliseconds. These are not pooled percentiles.

Including warmup and drift cells, the audit counts 1,530 runs, 3,420 activities
and callbacks, 6,480 first-attempt tasks and 14,850 business events. Typed results,
history counts and identities match. No unfinished run/task/attempt/activity,
non-first task/attempt, residual queue or failed job remains. The summed task
`repair_count` is **375**, all in fan-out cells; do not describe this batch as
zero repair/redispatch work. Fan-out repetition counters are published
32/45/44, disabled 35/36/34 and enabled 41/30/38, plus 40 in the final baseline.
Every ordinary cell has zero. This work remains included in measured CPU.

All enabled spans ended and were received: 4,456 / 4,456, including warmup.
Ordinary enabled cells each have 1,050 spans, 21,750 bytes of run metadata and
143,400 bytes of task metadata. Fan-out enabled cells have 440/429/437 spans,
435 bytes of run metadata and 102,813 bytes of task metadata each. These are
stored observability-field byte counts, not total database size or network
traffic. Activity-execution metadata is zero. Disabled/published cells produce
no spans or stored carrier metadata. No durable business payload/history field
was replaced by telemetry.

## Reader correction and remaining limits

The original analyzer rejected three actual callback elapsed values:
119.999219339, 119.999356686 and 119.999713308 seconds. Their original drivers
completed with all declared offers and results. Node's integer timer precision
does not guarantee an exact callback time. The corrected reader retains those
actual values, verifies the observation covers the final declared offer, and
requires **every cgroup counter interval to cover the full 120-second window**.
It neither rounds elapsed data nor rescales CPU. The new controls failed on the
prior reader and pass in the corrected 24-test analysis/probe suite. Original
samples, workloads, CPU targets and statistical method are unchanged. No cell
was rerun or relabeled as another original.

An earlier functional baseline completed business work but failed probe teardown;
it remains unsuccessful. A separate corrected lifecycle control passed before
this batch. This batch's original drivers all completed successfully. The
experiment host, key and raw data are disposable; the code and this readable
result are the retained outcome.

The encoded-baggage unit failure remains selected against the released OTel
dependency. Full tracing, migration/catalog integration and consumer acceptance
remain unfinished. These measurements do not authorize a release. Next source
work should investigate the enabled ordinary execution/export cost and improve
measurement sensitivity before considering a new, separately declared study.
No adaptive extra repetitions or relaxed targets are part of this result.
